hq_report_verdict: HQ's independently identified defect is CONFIRMED, not merely accepted. The R2 comment asserting that PyList_AsTuple consumes its input reference is false, and was introduced by me. Verified empirically on the governed interpreter: PyList_AsTuple leaves the input list's refcount delta at exactly 0, as does PySequence_Tuple, including for the empty list.

repaired.reported_defect: decide(): `ordered` was never released after PyList_AsTuple, leaking one list and, through it, its element references, on BOTH the success and the failure path. Repaired with an explicit Py_DECREF immediately after the conversion, before the NULL test, so one release covers both outcomes.
repaired.adjacent_temporary: compute_custody_hash released its owned rl and al lists only on the failure path, because Py_BuildValue's 'O' does not steal. Repaired to release on both paths.
repaired.self_inflicted_defect_removed: the unconditional Py_INCREF I added to trusted_canon in HQ245 was itself a permanent one-reference-per-call leak. PyObject_CallFunctionObjArgs already returns a NEW owned reference, so the extra INCREF was incorrect. It was invisible on the positive decide path because the canonicalised values there are interned strings costing zero pymalloc blocks, and visible only on the negative path where freshly allocated dicts cost real blocks. Removed. All 397 existing tests pass with it removed, so it was never load-bearing: the HQ245 EXC_BAD_ACCESS was caused by the separate borrowed-argument over-DECREF (MEM-002), not by this.
